title: Arrangement Tricks
intro: Arranging is mostly moving big blocks of time around without breaking anything. These tricks let you restructure a whole song without dragging regions one by one.

tips.t: Use the Arrangement track to move whole sections
tips.d: Open Global Tracks with G, enable the Arrangement track, and drop markers on your Verse, Chorus and Bridge. Now drag the Chorus marker and the entire section — every track, every automation point — moves with it.

src.label: Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Drag one arrangement marker onto another to swap sections
tips.d: Drag one arrangement marker directly over another and the two switch places, with all their content swapped. Every region, marker and automation point in each section goes with it, so you can try several song orders in moments.

src.label: Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: ⌥‑drag an arrangement marker to duplicate a section
tips.d: Hold ⌥ and drag any arrangement marker to copy that entire section, contents and all, to a new point in the timeline.

src.label: Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Delete a section and close the gap
tips.d: Select the arrangement marker and press Delete once — that removes the section's regions. Press Delete again and the marker goes too, pulling everything after it back to close the hole.

src.label: Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Set the locators around the gap you want, then choose Edit > Cut/Insert Time > Insert Silence Between Locators. A region that crosses the left locator is cut there, and the part after it moves to the right of the right locator. It's a quick way to add two bars to an intro.

src.label: macProVideo — Making Whole Project Edits in Logic Pro

Apple — Add or remove gaps in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Resize arrangement markers to fit your sections
tips.d: New arrangement markers always appear at the start of the project or after the last existing marker, eight bars long, regardless of the playhead position. So create the marker first, then drag its right edge left or right until it matches the section.

src.label: Apple — Add arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use aliases for parts that must stay identical
tips.d: Option-Shift-drag a MIDI region to where you want the alias to start. An alias is a reference to the original region, so when you change the original, every alias changes too. Use it for a part that has to repeat identically across the song.

src.label: macProVideo — Understanding Aliases in Logic Pro
Apple — Create MIDI aliases in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Make a folder out of a section
tips.d: Select every region in a section and choose Functions > Folder > Pack Folder from the Tracks area menu bar to pack them into a folder.

src.label: Apple — Pack and unpack folders in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Open the colour palette with ⌥C and give every chorus the same colour across all tracks. You can then read the arrangement at a glance from fully zoomed out.

src.label: Apple — Change the color of regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Track Stacks to collapse instrument families
tips.d: Select related tracks, create a Track Stack and choose Summing Stack. All the tracks in a summing stack send their audio to one shared auxiliary track, so a whole drum kit sits under a single stack.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro for Mac track stacks overview
Logic Studio Training — How To Organize Your Logic Pro Projects With Folder Track Stacks

tips.t: Loop an arrangement section with one key
tips.d: Select the regions that make up the section and press U (Set Rounded Locators by Regions/Events and Enable Cycle). Logic sets the locators around your selection, rounded to the nearest barlines, and turns Cycle on, so the section loops in time. Press ⌘U instead to set the locators exactly at the selection's edges.

src.label: macProVideo — 6 Logic Pro X Cycling Tips For A Faster Production Workflow

tips.t: Mute regions instead of deleting them while experimenting
tips.d: Click a region with the Mute tool, or select the regions and press Control-M. Muted regions turn grey with a dot before the name, so arrangement experiments become reversible without touching undo.

src.label: Apple — Mute and solo regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Keep a “graveyard” track at the bottom
tips.d: Make one muted, hidden track and drag every rejected idea onto it. Nothing is ever deleted, and the good version of that rejected idea is there when you need it three weeks later.

tips.t: Use markers for notes to self, not just sections
tips.d: The Marker track is one of the global tracks shown by default. Create a marker, then rename it “fix snare here” or “vocal comp needed”. Your to‑do list lives on the timeline instead of on paper.

src.label: Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac
